prose: A New York Times piece on the economics of AI in law firms: as AI makes lawyers more efficient, clients are asking the obvious question - where's my discount? The body was not captured (fetch error), so this summary rests on the headline.

On that basis: the billable hour meets its contradiction - if AI does in minutes what associates billed hours for, clients will refuse to pay for the difference, forcing firms toward flat fees, value pricing, or a fight over who keeps the productivity gains. Which firms and numbers feature is unknown from the capture.
highlights: NYT: AI efficiency has law clients asking 'where's my discount?'
The billable hour collides with AI productivity gains
At stake: who keeps the surplus - firm or client - and the shift to alternative fee models
Body not captured; firms and figures unknown
